subject: COM
label: Grade 07
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 07 Computing, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: HTML basics
modules.outcome: build a simple web page with text, images and links
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'HTML basics', taught in a way that is with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. The target is clear: build a simple web page with text, images and links. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: See it: watch or try the skill in 'HTML basics' on a teacher screen or a safe device.
Name the parts: write the key words and what each part does.
Use it: build a simple web page with text, images and links. Save your work in a named file or folder.
Test and fix: run it, find one fault, correct it, and note what you changed.
modules.example:
Solved:

About. CSS: p { color: blue; } makes paragraphs blue. Method: Model run for 'HTML basics'. Goal in one sentence. Plan: list the steps in order before touching the device. Do: follow the plan, saving after each step. Test: try normal input and one unusual input. Fix: change one thing and test again. Share: show a partner and explain it. What a good answer looks like: it works for normal input, steps match the plan, and the learner can explain each part. Online safety rules apply at all times.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Build a simple web page with text, images and links: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.

ladder: L1: use a device safely; click, type and draw.
L2: create documents; follow simple instructions in blocks.
L3: spreadsheets, algorithms and simple programs.
L5: software design, databases and security.
